question.text: A particle is projected from the earth's surface with a velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> at an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>θ</mi></math> with the horizontal. After <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> it just clears a wall <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> high. What is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>55</mn><mo> </mo><mi>sin</mi><mi>θ</mi></math>? (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
Using equation of motion in y-dir s=ut+12at2

Height after 2 s,

h=5=50 sinθt-12gt2

5 = 50 sin θ 2 - 1 2 · 10 · 2 2

25 100 = sin θ

sin θ = 1 4

55 sinθ=554=13.75
